reasoning: The question asks about a Russian crewed aircraft being shot down in NATO airspace by March 19, 2026 - just 13 days from the forecast date. Since the 2015 Turkey incident, NATO has generally avoided shooting down Russian aircraft despite numerous violations, preferring to escort them out. The September 2025 Estonian incident followed this pattern. For a shootdown to occur in the next 13 days would require either a significant escalation in Russian behavior or a dramatic change in NATO rules of engagement. Neither seems imminent based on the pattern of de-escalation. The short timeframe makes this very unlikely.
